UPSTREAM: mainboard/google/reef: Set edge triggered interrupt for GPIO_22 EC sets the logic level based on outstanding wake events. When GPIO_22 is configured as a level triggered interrupt, the events are not cleared from the interrupt handler. Hence, we'd just be re-signalling over and over causing an interrupt storm upon lid open. So, GPIO_22 needs to be configured as EDGE_SINGLE instead of LEVEL. CHROMIUM: drm/bridge/analogix: Allow master driver to cleanup in unbind Since we take the ownership of drvdata, the master driver does not have any means of accessing its own data from unbind callback and all it can do is calling the analogix unbind callback. However it might be necessary to do some clean up in the master driver before we really unbind the analogix part (such as PSR unregister in Rockchip case), so this patch provides a plat_data->cleanup() callback which is called at the beginning of analogix_dp_unbind(). eve: Add support for 3 color PWM controlled LEDs Eve has two 3 color PWM controlled LEDs. This CL adds basic support for these LEDs so that they can be set to off, red, green, or blue. In addition, the LED policy from Kevin is appropriated. In S0 the LEDs will be blue. In S3/S5 if no charger is connected, then the LEDs are off If a charger is connected and the charge level is less than a threshold, both LEDs are set to red. When the charge level gets above a certain level or if the charge state is idle, then the LEDs are set to green. [autotest] Use provisioning in place of parameterized jobs. Formerly, when the create_job() RPC was passed an image for testing, the handling was to create a special parameterized job that would invoke autoserv with the `--image` option, so that the build would be installed directly. However, the specified `image` parameter couldn't be passed to shards, so the feature could only work for DUTs assigned to the autotest master. This changes handling such that when an image is specified at job creation time, the image is converted to a `cros-version` label dependency. This allows the specified build information to be passed to shards. Additionally, after this change, the code relating to parameterized jobs becomes dead (along with the related image specification/installation code), enabling additional code cleanup. BUG=chromium:628694 TEST=create jobs with images via web UI and CLI in a local instance Change-Id: Ic01c7bdbbc6ded537a9f4808844b2d7d32663494 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/433364 Commit-Ready: Allen Li <ayatane@chromium.org> Tested-by: Richard Barnette <jrbarnette@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Allen Li <ayatane@chromium.org>

Update Kevin TP config to pass noise test This CL updated the touchpad firmware config for Kevin such that it passes our electrical noise test. The touchpad was struggling to pass all of our spec at once and this introduces a small regression in finger separation (when two fingers are close together it gets hard to separate them) but passes the noise test. This is a tradeoff, but we've already had users getting hit by electrical noise and that can thoroughly render a touchpad useless, whereas finger separation can be compensated for more easily by the user if they run into issues. As such, this config is preferable. Hopefully we'll get a config that passes our whole spec at once, but for now at least this is an improvement. BUG=chrome-os-partner:62157 TEST=emerged and deployed on my Kevin. The config was tested by Allion and passed everything but the finger separation tests. Manual testing and feedback from dogfooders seems that this config will be preferred. Update Caroline TP config to pass noise test This CL updated the touchpad firmware config for Caroline such that it passes our electrical noise test. The touchpad was struggling to pass all of our spec at once and this introduces a small regression in finger separation (when two fingers are close together it gets hard to separate them) but passes the noise test. This is a tradeoff, but we've already had users getting hit by electrical noise and that can thoroughly render a touchpad useless, whereas finger separation can be compensated for more easily by the user if they run into issues. As such, this config is preferable. Hopefully we'll get a config that passes our whole spec at once, but for now at least this is an improvement. BUG=chrome-os-partner:62157 TEST=emerged and deployed on my Caroline. The config was tested by Allion and passed everything but the finger separation tests. Manual testing and feedback from dogfooders seems that this config will be preferred.
